svg.title: GLP-1 drugs and alcohol: what has actually been tested
svg.desc: GLP-1 drugs and alcohol: what has actually been tested. Approved for alcohol use disorder?: No GLP-1 drug is approved for it; all uses for drinking are investigational. Verdict: Not approved. Animal studies: Rodents drink less, binge less and relapse less on several GLP-1-type drugs. Verdict: Consistent. Randomized trials in people: Six small trials (48 to 151 people, 8 to 26 weeks); three met their main goal, two missed. Verdict: Mixed, small. Best single trial: Lancet 2026: heavy drinking days fell 13.7 points more than placebo, in AUD plus obesity. Verdict: Positive. Health-record studies: Fewer alcohol-related hospital visits and relapses; cannot prove cause. Verdict: Consistent, confounded. Does weight loss explain it?: In one study the drinking drop lost significance after adjusting for weight change. Verdict: Open question. After stopping: In one Swedish study the hospital benefit faded 6 to 12 months after stopping. Verdict: May fade. Large trials: Lilly brenipatide (2 x 1,100 people, results early 2028); VA semaglutide (622). Verdict: Under way.
